chapter: After the Army: JATP, clubs and first Europe trips
title: Nine months in postwar Paris
summary: After Panassie hired a French rhythm section, he stayed nine months, learned about postwar Parisian life and picked up slang.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Yes. I still might have a sea stomache, I don't know. But I know that boat used to rock and all I'd just roll with it, I hever would get, I never got dizzy. The only time you get dizzy is drinking that red wine that they keep putting in front of you for dinner. You drink red wine with the dinner, before the dinner and after dinner and then you try to get back to your cabin. Parnassus So anyway, when we got to France, met us and he had hired a tenor player, an alto player and a bass player.
Yes. They were all French. So now that makes us have six. Me and Bish, Step and a tenor and an alto, oh a piano. He had also

a piano. So we made a little tour over there and I stayed there about nine months. I was really going to stay about six weeks. But you see, Paris at that time, it wasn't too long after the War was over, '49 the War had just been over and they were still active and whatever we took over there, like we took soap like and cigarettes and things/that, we could get anything we wanted, mostly, you know. Because they were still short on everything.

So I stayed nine months. And I learned a lot about Parisan people that are not rich, you know like they didn't have ice boxes so they kept everything out on the window sill. When Christmas time would come if they could afford to buy a goose or turkey they didn't have no place to cook it. They could take it to the bakery and give the guy a little extra change to sneak it in there with the bread.
Yes, but we didn't do it, we you could could have cooked it but actually, we had a baker just
across the street. But you could get a turkey cooked better in those great big ovens than you could in an ordinary one.
Well, I know that's what they did. That's what they did in France. Just sneak it right on in there with the bread and pick them up a couple of hours later.

Everybody took a bath in the bath house because they didn't have, a lot of them didn't have bath tubs. So I was just glad that I was there in all seasons. In the summer when it's hot, nobody is in Paris in the summer time. They go to the mountains or the sea shore.
But I was glad because I learned more about speaking French and things that are not in the book, you know, slang.
